blocks.zh: 第零章：導論、適用範圍與潔淨室分級
blocks.en: Section 0: Introduction, Scope, and Cleanroom Classification

blocks.zh: 本章學習目標
blocks.en: Learning Objectives

blocks.zh: 理解 USP 〈1116〉 的定位：資訊性章節（Informational），非強制性標準 — 但實務上為 EM 計畫設計的核心依據
blocks.en: Understand the position of USP <1116>: an informational chapter, not a mandatory standard - but in practice the core reference for EM program design

blocks.zh: 區分 Aseptic（無菌操作）與 Sterile（無菌）的概念差異，理解為何「零汙染期望」在技術上不可行
blocks.en: Distinguish "aseptic" from "sterile", and understand why an expectation of zero contamination is technically unachievable

blocks.zh: 掌握 ISO 14644-1 潔淨室分級（ISO 5–8）與傳統 Federal Standard 209E 的對應關係
blocks.en: Understand the ISO 14644-1 cleanroom classes (ISO 5-8) and how they map to the legacy Federal Standard 209E classes

blocks.zh: 認識先進無菌技術（Isolator, Closed RABS, BFS）與傳統潔淨室在汙染控制上的根本差異
blocks.en: Recognize the fundamental difference in contamination control between advanced aseptic technologies (isolators, closed RABS, BFS) and conventional cleanrooms

blocks.zh: 理解環境監測的本質限制：半定量、無法證明或否定無菌、取樣本身帶來汙染風險
blocks.en: Understand the inherent limits of environmental monitoring: it is semi-quantitative, it can neither prove nor disprove sterility, and the act of sampling itself carries a contamination risk

blocks.zh: Introduction & Scope — 導論與適用範圍
blocks.en: Introduction & Scope

blocks.zh: 原文內容 Original Text
blocks.en: Original Text

blocks.zh: 導師解析 Tutorial Commentary
blocks.en: Tutorial Commentary

blocks.zh: 核心概念：Aseptic vs Sterile
blocks.en: Key Concept: Aseptic vs Sterile

blocks.zh: 這是 USP 〈1116〉 開宗明義最重要的區分：
blocks.en: This is the most important distinction USP <1116> makes at the outset:

blocks.zh: Sterile（無菌） — 完全沒有活的微生物，是一個「狀態」的描述
blocks.en: Sterile - the complete absence of viable microorganisms; it describes a "state"

blocks.zh: Aseptic（無菌操作） — 是一個「過程」的描述，透過排除微生物來防止汙染
blocks.en: Aseptic - describes a "process" that prevents contamination by excluding microorganisms

blocks.zh: 在實際製藥環境中，aseptic processing 不可能達到真正的 sterile 狀態 — 因為有人在場就一定會釋放微生物。這就是為什麼 USP 強調「零汙染期望在技術上不可行」。
blocks.en: In a real pharmaceutical environment, aseptic processing can never reach a truly sterile state, because wherever people are present, microorganisms are shed. This is why USP stresses that an expectation of zero contamination is technically unachievable.

blocks.zh: Cross-reference：EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) Section 4.3 也明確表達相同觀點，並要求在 CCS（Contamination Control Strategy）中納入此風險認知。
blocks.en: Cross-reference: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) Section 4.3 expresses the same view and requires this risk awareness to be built into the CCS (Contamination Control Strategy).

blocks.zh: 比喻說明：手術室 vs 實驗室
blocks.en: Analogy: Operating Room vs Laboratory

blocks.zh: 想像一間手術室：即使使用最先進的空氣過濾系統和最嚴格的消毒程序，只要有外科醫師和護理人員在場，環境就不可能是「完全無菌」的。手術室的目標不是達到零微生物，而是將汙染風險控制在不會對病人造成感染的水準。
blocks.en: Picture an operating room. Even with the most advanced air filtration and the strictest disinfection procedures, the environment can never be "completely sterile" as long as surgeons and nurses are present. The goal of an operating room is not zero microorganisms, but keeping contamination risk to a level that does not cause infection in the patient.

blocks.zh: 無菌充填室也一樣 — 目標是「風險可接受」而非「絕對無菌」。這個認知對設計 EM 計畫至關重要：我們監測的目的是確認「控制狀態」，不是「證明無菌」。
blocks.en: An aseptic filling room is the same: the goal is "acceptable risk", not "absolute sterility". This understanding is critical when designing an EM program: the purpose of monitoring is to confirm the "state of control", not to "prove sterility".

blocks.zh: 重點提示：EM 數值的法律定位
blocks.en: Key Point: The Regulatory Standing of EM Values

blocks.zh: USP 〈1116〉 是 Informational Chapter（資訊性章節），不同於 USP 〈71〉（Sterility Tests）這類有法律約束力的 Official Chapter。然而：
blocks.en: USP <1116> is an Informational Chapter, unlike legally binding Official Chapters such as USP <71> (Sterility Tests). However:

blocks.zh: FDA 在 Aseptic Processing Guidance (2004) 中直接引用 〈1116〉 的概念
blocks.en: The FDA Aseptic Processing Guidance (2004) directly cites concepts from <1116>

blocks.zh: EU GMP Annex 1 Table 7/8 的 alert/action limits 與 〈1116〉 的理念一致
blocks.en: The alert/action limits in EU GMP Annex 1 Tables 7/8 are consistent with the thinking in <1116>

blocks.zh: PDA TR13（Fundamentals of an EM Program）以 〈1116〉 為科學基礎
blocks.en: PDA TR13 (Fundamentals of an EM Program) uses <1116> as its scientific basis

blocks.zh: 每次 FDA/EMA 查廠，EM program 都是必查項目
blocks.en: The EM program is a must-review item in every FDA/EMA inspection

blocks.zh: 所以實務上，雖然 〈1116〉 的數值不是「法定限值」，但你的 EM 計畫如果與其建議嚴重偏離，稽查員會要求你提出科學理據。
blocks.en: So in practice, although the values in <1116> are not "legal limits", if your EM program deviates significantly from its recommendations, inspectors will ask you for a scientific justification.

blocks.zh: 重點提示：監測本身的矛盾
blocks.en: Key Point: The Paradox of Monitoring

blocks.zh: USP 提出一個深刻的悖論：環境監測會增加汙染風險。因為：
blocks.en: USP raises a profound paradox: environmental monitoring increases contamination risk. This is because:

blocks.zh: 取樣需要人員進入潔淨區域（增加微生物釋放）
blocks.en: Sampling requires personnel to enter the cleanroom area (increasing microbial shedding)

blocks.zh: 取樣器材的放置和操作可能干擾氣流
blocks.en: Placing and operating sampling equipment can disrupt airflow

blocks.zh: 接觸取樣可能造成假陽性
blocks.en: Contact sampling can produce false positives

blocks.zh: 所以 〈1116〉 明確表示「在 ISO 5 區域，密集監測是不必要的」— 這與很多人的直覺相反。在 CDMO 中，這是設計 EM 計畫時需要與客戶和 QA 團隊溝通的重要議題。
blocks.en: That is why <1116> states explicitly that "intensive monitoring is unnecessary in ISO 5 areas" - the opposite of what many people expect. In a CDMO, this is an important topic to discuss with clients and the QA team when designing the EM program.

blocks.zh: 練習思考 Practice Questions
blocks.en: Practice Questions

blocks.zh: 如果你的 CDMO 客戶要求在 ISO 5 充填區域每 30 分鐘進行一次 active air sampling，你會如何回應？引用 〈1116〉 的哪些觀點？
blocks.en: If your CDMO client asks for active air sampling every 30 minutes in the ISO 5 filling area, how would you respond? Which points in <1116> would you cite?

blocks.zh: 為什麼 USP 特別強調 〈1116〉 的數值不是「限值或規格」？這對你設計 EM alert/action levels 有什麼影響？
blocks.en: Why does USP stress that the values in <1116> are not "limits or specifications"? How does this affect the way you design EM alert/action levels?

blocks.zh: 比較 〈1116〉（Informational）與 〈71〉（Official）的法律地位差異。在 FDA 查廠時，兩者的角色分別是什麼？
blocks.en: Compare the legal status of <1116> (Informational) and <71> (Official). What role does each play during an FDA inspection?

blocks.zh: Advanced Aseptic Technologies — 先進無菌技術
blocks.en: Advanced Aseptic Technologies

blocks.zh: 核心概念：技術階層與汙染風險
blocks.en: Key Concept: Technology Hierarchy and Contamination Risk

blocks.zh: USP 建立了一個清楚的無菌技術階層（從最低到最高汙染風險）：
blocks.en: USP establishes a clear hierarchy of aseptic technologies (from lowest to highest contamination risk):

blocks.zh: Isolator — 最佳分離，自動去汙染，人員完全隔離
blocks.en: Isolator - the best separation, automated decontamination, personnel fully isolated

blocks.zh: Closed RABS — 操作中不開啟，僅使用手套/半身衣操作
blocks.en: Closed RABS - not opened during operation; interventions only through gloves/half-suits

blocks.zh: Open RABS — 允許開放式人員介入，等同傳統潔淨室
blocks.en: Open RABS - allows open personnel interventions, equivalent to a conventional cleanroom

blocks.zh: Conventional Cleanroom — 人員在 ISO 5 區域直接操作
blocks.en: Conventional Cleanroom - personnel work directly in the ISO 5 area

blocks.zh: Cross-reference：EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) Section 4.18–4.22 對 RABS 和 Isolator 有更詳細的定義，並明確要求新設施優先考慮 separative technologies。
blocks.en: Cross-reference: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) Sections 4.18-4.22 define RABS and isolators in more detail and explicitly require that separative technologies be considered first for new facilities.

blocks.zh: 比喻說明：廚房防蟲的不同策略
blocks.en: Analogy: Different Strategies for Keeping Bugs Out of the Kitchen

blocks.zh: 傳統潔淨室就像一個開放式廚房 — 再怎麼打掃、再怎麼穿乾淨制服，廚師身上還是會帶進灰塵和微生物。
blocks.en: A conventional cleanroom is like an open kitchen: however much you clean and however clean the uniforms, the cook still brings in dust and microorganisms.

blocks.zh: Isolator 則像把食物放在密封的玻璃櫃裡 — 透過手套從外面操作。即使廚房不是 100% 乾淨，食物被汙染的風險大幅降低。
blocks.en: An isolator is like keeping the food in a sealed glass cabinet and handling it from outside through gloves. Even if the kitchen is not 100% clean, the risk of contaminating the food is greatly reduced.

blocks.zh: Open RABS 就像有門的櫃子 — 如果你偶爾把門打開伸手進去，它的保護效果就和沒有櫃子差不多了。
blocks.en: An open RABS is like a cabinet with a door: if you open the door now and then and reach in, its protection is little better than having no cabinet at all.

blocks.zh: 重點提示：CDMO 技術選型
blocks.en: Key Point: Technology Selection in a CDMO

blocks.zh: 對 CDMO 的直接影響：
blocks.en: Direct impact on a CDMO:

blocks.zh: 使用 Isolator/Closed RABS 的產線，EM 要求更嚴格（contamination recovery rate <0.1%），但因為人員隔離更好，實際汙染率極低
blocks.en: Lines using an isolator/closed RABS carry stricter EM expectations (contamination recovery rate <0.1%), but because personnel are better separated, the actual contamination rate is extremely low

blocks.zh: 傳統潔淨室的 EM 要求相對「寬鬆」（ISO 5 <1%），但實際操作更依賴人員紀律
blocks.en: Conventional cleanrooms have comparatively "looser" EM expectations (ISO 5 <1%), but actual operation depends far more on personnel discipline

blocks.zh: FDA Aseptic Processing Guidance 鼓勵使用 isolator 技術
blocks.en: The FDA Aseptic Processing Guidance encourages the use of isolator technology

blocks.zh: White Raven（歐洲 CDMO）的 SA25 filling machine 就是 Isolator-based 設計
blocks.en: The SA25 filling machine at White Raven (a European CDMO) is an isolator-based design

blocks.zh: 你的 CDMO 同時有 Isolator 產線和傳統潔淨室產線。在設計 EM 計畫時，兩條產線的取樣頻率和判定標準應該如何不同？
blocks.en: Your CDMO has both isolator lines and conventional cleanroom lines. When designing the EM program, how should the sampling frequency and acceptance criteria differ between the two?

blocks.zh: 一家客戶堅持在 Open RABS 操作中使用與 Closed RABS 相同的 EM 標準。這合理嗎？為什麼？
blocks.en: A client insists on applying the same EM standards to open RABS operations as to closed RABS. Is that reasonable? Why?

blocks.zh: Clean Room Classification for Aseptic Processing Environments — 無菌操作環境的潔淨室分級
blocks.en: Clean Room Classification for Aseptic Processing Environments

blocks.zh: 核心概念：粒子數 vs 微生物數
blocks.en: Key Concept: Particle Counts vs Microbial Counts

blocks.zh: USP 提出一個經常被誤解的觀點：非活性粒子數與微生物汙染之間的關係不是直接的。
blocks.en: USP makes a frequently misunderstood point: the relationship between non-viable particle counts and microbial contamination is not direct.

blocks.zh: 人員是微生物汙染的唯一顯著來源
blocks.en: People are the only significant source of microbial contamination

blocks.zh: 設備是非活性粒子的另一個重要來源
blocks.en: Equipment is another important source of non-viable particles

blocks.zh: 因此「粒子數低就表示微生物少」只在人員是粒子主要來源時才成立
blocks.en: So "low particle counts mean few microorganisms" holds only when people are the main source of particles

blocks.zh: 這就是為什麼 EM 計畫必須同時包含非活性粒子監測和微生物監測兩個部分 — 它們提供不同的資訊。
blocks.en: This is why an EM program must include both non-viable particle monitoring and microbiological monitoring - they provide different information.

blocks.zh: 比喻說明：換氣次數與排風扇
blocks.en: Analogy: Air Changes and Exhaust Fans

blocks.zh: 換氣次數（ACH）就像房間裡的排風扇功率：
blocks.en: Air changes per hour (ACH) are like the power of the exhaust fan in a room:

blocks.zh: ISO 8（20 ACH）— 普通浴室排風扇，慢慢帶走濕氣
blocks.en: ISO 8 (20 ACH) - an ordinary bathroom fan, slowly carrying away moisture

blocks.zh: ISO 7（50 ACH）— 油煙機，快速排除廚房油煙
blocks.en: ISO 7 (50 ACH) - a range hood, quickly clearing cooking fumes

blocks.zh: ISO 5（100+ ACH）— 工業級排氣系統，幾乎是持續吹拂的清潔氣流
blocks.en: ISO 5 (100+ ACH) - an industrial-grade exhaust system, an almost continuous stream of clean air

blocks.zh: 重點不只是換氣頻率，而是氣流方向 — ISO 5 區域需要 unidirectional flow（單向氣流），就像風從天花板往地板吹，把汙染物帶離產品表面。
blocks.en: The point is not only how often the air is changed but the direction of airflow - an ISO 5 area needs unidirectional flow, like wind blowing from ceiling to floor, carrying contaminants away from the product surface.

blocks.zh: FDA 查廠時使用 ISO 分級，EMA 查廠時使用 EU Grade。作為 CDMO，你的 EM SOP 應該使用哪套分級系統？如何在一份 SOP 中同時滿足兩個市場？
blocks.en: The FDA uses ISO classes in inspections, while the EMA uses EU Grades. As a CDMO, which classification system should your EM SOP use? How can one SOP satisfy both markets?

blocks.zh: 你的 ISO 5 充填區域的非活性粒子計數持續合格，但微生物回收率突然上升。根據 〈1116〉 的觀點，這暗示什麼原因？
blocks.en: The non-viable particle counts in your ISO 5 filling area keep passing, but the microbial recovery rate suddenly rises. According to <1116>, what does this suggest?

blocks.zh: 重點提示：ISO vs EU GMP Grade 對照
blocks.en: Key Point: ISO vs EU GMP Grade Comparison

blocks.zh: USP 使用 ISO 14644-1 分級。FDA 也使用 ISO 分級。但 EU GMP Annex 1 使用 Grade A/B/C/D 系統。CDMO 必須同時理解兩套系統：
blocks.en: USP uses ISO 14644-1 classification, and the FDA also uses ISO classes. EU GMP Annex 1, however, uses the Grade A/B/C/D system. A CDMO must understand both systems:

blocks.zh: 注意：EU GMP Grade B in operation 對應 ISO 7，但 Grade B at rest 對應 ISO 5。這是 CDMO 最常搞混的地方。
blocks.en: Note: EU GMP Grade B in operation corresponds to ISO 7, but Grade B at rest corresponds to ISO 5. This is what CDMOs most often confuse.

blocks.zh: Importance of a Microbiological Evaluation Program — 微生物評估計畫的重要性
blocks.en: Importance of a Microbiological Evaluation Program

blocks.zh: 核心概念：EM 的真正價值
blocks.en: Key Concept: The True Value of EM

blocks.zh: USP 用了大量篇幅解釋 EM 的限制和真正用途，這些觀點是理解整個 〈1116〉 的基石：
blocks.en: USP devotes considerable space to the limitations and true purpose of EM; these points are the foundation for understanding the whole of <1116>:

blocks.zh: EM 是半定量的 — 我們無法精確量化環境中的微生物數量
blocks.en: EM is semi-quantitative - we cannot precisely quantify the number of microorganisms in the environment

blocks.zh: 零回收不等於無汙染 — 只是低於偵測極限
blocks.en: Zero recovery does not mean no contamination - it only means results are below the detection limit

blocks.zh: EM 不能證明無菌 — 它只能確認「控制狀態」的一致性
blocks.en: EM cannot prove sterility - it can only confirm the consistency of the "state of control"

blocks.zh: 趨勢比單一結果更重要 — 監測的價值在於偵測變化
blocks.en: Trends matter more than single results - the value of monitoring lies in detecting change

blocks.zh: Cross-reference：PDA TR13 Section 3.0 和 PDA TR88 都強調相同的哲學 — EM 是 CCS 的一個「確認工具」，不是品質保證的替代品。
blocks.en: Cross-reference: PDA TR13 Section 3.0 and PDA TR88 both emphasize the same philosophy - EM is a "verification tool" within the CCS, not a substitute for quality assurance.

blocks.zh: 比喻說明：體溫計的隱喻
blocks.en: Analogy: The Thermometer

blocks.zh: EM 就像量體溫 — 體溫正常不代表你沒有任何疾病（可能有病但還沒發燒），體溫升高也不一定代表你感染了（可能剛運動完）。
blocks.en: EM is like taking your temperature. A normal reading does not mean you have no illness (you may be sick without a fever yet), and a raised reading does not necessarily mean you are infected (you may have just exercised).

blocks.zh: 但如果你每天量體溫，連續三天都比平常高 0.5°C，這個「趨勢」就值得注意了。EM 的價值也在這裡 — 不是單一數據點，而是持續的模式和趨勢。
blocks.en: But if you take your temperature every day and it is 0.5°C above normal for three days running, that "trend" deserves attention. This is the value of EM too - not a single data point, but continuing patterns and trends.

blocks.zh: 重點提示：取樣時機
blocks.en: Key Point: Timing of Sampling

blocks.zh: USP 明確要求在正常生產操作期間取樣 — 材料在現場、製程進行中、所有人員在位。這與某些工廠在「最佳條件」下取樣（如人員最少、設備靜止時）的做法相矛盾。
blocks.en: USP explicitly requires sampling during normal production operations - with materials on site, the process running, and all personnel in place. This contradicts the practice in some plants of sampling under "best conditions" (for example, minimum personnel and idle equipment).

blocks.zh: 對 CDMO 的啟示：如果你的 EM 數據都是在非生產狀態下取得的，FDA 查廠員可能會質疑這些數據是否反映真實的生產風險。
blocks.en: Implication for a CDMO: If all your EM data are obtained in non-production states, FDA inspectors may question whether those data reflect real production risk.

blocks.zh: 你的 ISO 5 區域連續 6 個月的空氣取樣都是零回收。你可以因此降低取樣頻率嗎？引用 〈1116〉 支持你的論點。
blocks.en: The air sampling results in your ISO 5 area have shown zero recovery for 6 consecutive months. Can you therefore reduce the sampling frequency? Cite <1116> to support your argument.

blocks.zh: 為什麼 USP 說「EM 是半定量的」？列舉三個導致 EM 無法精確量化的技術限制。
blocks.en: Why does USP say "EM is semi-quantitative"? List three technical limitations that prevent EM from being precisely quantitative.

blocks.zh: 本節重點回顧 Section Summary
blocks.en: Section Summary

blocks.zh: USP 〈1116〉 定位：Informational Chapter — 不具法律強制力，但實務上是 FDA/EMA 稽查 EM 計畫的核心參考依據
blocks.en: Position of USP <1116>: Informational Chapter - not legally binding, but in practice the core reference for FDA/EMA inspection of EM programs

blocks.zh: Aseptic ≠ Sterile：無菌操作是風險控制的過程，不是達到絕對無菌的結果。零汙染期望在技術上不可行
blocks.en: Aseptic ≠ Sterile: aseptic processing is a process of risk control, not a result of reaching absolute sterility. An expectation of zero contamination is technically unachievable

blocks.zh: 先進技術優先：Isolator > Closed RABS > Open RABS > Conventional Cleanroom（EU GMP Annex 1 要求新設施優先採用 separative technologies）
blocks.en: Advanced technologies first: Isolator > Closed RABS > Open RABS > Conventional Cleanroom (EU GMP Annex 1 requires new facilities to give priority to separative technologies)

blocks.zh: 分級對照：ISO 5 = Class 100 = Grade A；ISO 7 = Class 10,000 = Grade C (at rest)；ISO 8 = Class 100,000 = Grade D
blocks.en: Classification comparison: ISO 5 = Class 100 = Grade A; ISO 7 = Class 10,000 = Grade C (at rest); ISO 8 = Class 100,000 = Grade D

blocks.zh: EM 本質限制：半定量、無法證明無菌、取樣本身增加汙染風險 — EM 的真正價值在於趨勢監測和控制狀態確認
blocks.en: Inherent limits of EM: semi-quantitative, cannot prove sterility, and sampling itself adds contamination risk - the true value of EM lies in trend monitoring and confirming the state of control

blocks.zh: 取樣原則：必須在正常生產操作條件下取樣，才能獲得有意義的數據
blocks.en: Sampling principle: samples must be taken under normal production conditions to obtain meaningful data
